newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble earnings rose 16 percent in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble earnings rose 16 percent in quarter.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co. said Thursday it earned $881 million in the latest quarter, an increase of 16 percent from a year earlier as sales grew 2 percent.

The maker of Ivory soap, Tide detergent and Pampers disposable diapers said the earnings equalled $1.26 a share for its third quarter ended on March 31, up from $1.07 a share a year earlier, or $760 million. Sales grew to $8.77 billion from $8.59 billion.
Procter & Gamble said sales measured by unit volume rose 4 percent but because of the stronger value of the dollar against foreign currencies sales measured in dollars grew just 2 percent.

Wall Street analysts surveyed by First Call had expected Procter & Gamble to earn $1.23 a share. Its stock rose $1.375 in early trading but later gave back the gains and was off 25 cents at $125.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We are genuinely pleased with our continued progress on margins and net earnings," said John E. Pepper, chairman. "At the same time, we still need to make additional progress in the areas of volume and sales growth and are in the process of expanding a number of product initiatives which will be important contributors to this growth."

The company said unit volume in North America grew 2 percent, largely on the strength of the laundry and snacks categories. In addition to Tide, Procter & Gamble makes Cheer and Bold detergent and Hawaiian Punch snack drinks.
In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, unit volume grew 9 percent, but the strong dollar meant revenues rose just 3 percent, the company said.
While sales in Asia were flat, income in the region increased by 37 percent due to a better product mix and higher prices. Sales to China rose more than 10 percent, Procter & Gamble said.
Income from Latin America jumped 53 percent, reflecting price changes and the sale of unprofitable brands, it said.
